speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe your symptoms, specifically focusing on the onset and characteristics of your diarrhea?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent levofloxacin use and the high frequency of watery stools, I am concerned about Clostridioides difficile infection. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Test_for_C._difficile_toxin

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial test result was inconclusive, so I need to look for other signs of severity. Do you have a fever, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: To assess for severe disease, I need to know your current temperature and whether your white blood cell count is elevated. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL, Total_Count_WBC: 13,400/mm3, Differential_Count: Neutrophils: 80%, Lymphocytes: 15%, Monocytes: 5%

speaker: Doctor
text: Your elevated white blood cell count of 13,400/mm3 strongly supports the suspicion of C. difficile infection despite the inconclusive initial toxin test. I will order a more specific test to confirm the diagnosis and check for signs of colonic dilation. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Test_for_C._difficile_toxin_GDHA, Abdominal_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan is reassuring as it rules out toxic megacolon or severe colitis complications. Given the high clinical suspicion based on antibiotic exposure, leukocytosis, and symptoms, I will proceed with treatment for C. difficile infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection
